plots.title: Selected tissue-volume checkpoints
plots.scope: Selected global evidence across human, mouse, and fruit fly datasets; not an exhaustive inventory or worldwide cumulative volume. Sample bounds, imaged volume, and neuropil volume are not interchangeable. Reconstruction completeness varies; no cross-dataset lines, sums, or global growth rate. Values converted from mm³ ÷ 1,000; ≈ denotes approximate sample bounds.

Connectomics imaging throughput over tim.summary: Measured acquisition examples at explicitly different resolutions. These do not yet measure sustained end-to-end reconstruction throughput.

plots.title: Selected EM acquisition rates
plots.scope: Different protocols; acquisition only. Derived from reported dimensions, elapsed time, or montage count. > is a lower bound, not an exact rate.

points.label: Enhanced FIB-SEM, Drosophila optic lobe
points.sourceTitle: Enhanced FIB-SEM systems for large-volume 3D imaging
points.quote: To evaluate the suitability of the customized FIB-SEM system for imaging even larger volumes, the *Drosophila* optic lobe, including medulla, lobula, and lobula plate, was imaged at 8 × 8 × 8 nm3 voxel resolution over a 100 day period, yielding a final four terabyte image volume of about 180 × 100 × 50 µm3 (50 µm in the direction of the FIB beam), shown in Figure 3.
points.note: Real 100-day acquisition, includes documented interruptions. Approximate final bounding volume, NOT quality-mask volume. Excludes upstream preparation and downstream reconstruction; one instrument; 8×8×8 nm voxels. Derivation: {"formula": "180*100*50 / 1e9 / 100", "input_units": "um3 / um3-per-mm3 / days", "basis": "reported final dimensions and actual elapsed acquisition period"}

points.label: autoTEM demonstrated montage production per microscope
points.sourceTitle: A petascale automated imaging pipeline for mapping neuronal circuits with high-throughput transmission electron microscopy
points.quote: More than 70 montages, each 1 mm2, could be imaged per day per scope.
points.note: LOWER BOUND (>70 montages/day); 1 mm2 section ROI × nominal 40 nm section thickness. Nominal montage slab volume, not valid-tissue mask or whole-pipeline rate. Section preparation and downstream alignment/reconstruction excluded; 4 nm pixels. Derivation: {"formula": "70 * 1 mm2 * (40 / 1e6) mm", "basis": "reported daily montage count, montage area and nominal thickness"}

Cost to map 1 cm³ over time.gapReason: Imaging components, research grants and estimated whole-brain budgets omit different costs. A realized imaging + compute + storage + proofreading total at a common quality threshold is still needed.

Automated reconstruction accuracy over t.summary: One published benchmark snapshot—not a historical accuracy trend. nERL is normalized expected run length, not percent of voxels correct.

plots.title: PATHFINDER v1: axon tracing benchmark
plots.scope: 2025 preprint v1; mouse unmyelinated axons, one fixed ground-truth set. Publication year does not establish the evaluation date.

points.label: PATHFINDER v1, unmyelinated mouse cortical axons
points.dateLabel: 2025 · version-1 preprint posting year; not an independently dated evaluation event
points.sourceTitle: Accelerating Neuron Reconstruction with PATHFINDER
points.quote: The segmentation variant optimized to minimize the total number of axon split and merge errors showed a normalized expected run length (nERL) of 94.2% (Table 1).
points.note: Preprint benchmark snapshot; NOT percent correctly segmented voxels. nERL = ERL / maximum ERL of this ground-truth set. Mouse IBEAM-mSEM, 80.4×84.8×99.2 um3; unmyelinated axons, 4,284 mm total path. Evaluation excludes a boundary margin for splits and uses node thresholds; no matched longitudinal series assembled.

Automated reconstruction accuracy over t.gapReason: No matched multi-year evaluation series was verified.

Human tissue preservation quality over t.gapReason: The reviewed 2025 human brain-bank study says traceability could not be rigorously quantified. Image artifact area and visible synapses are not fractions of connections traceable.

points.quote: The Machine Intelligence from Cortical Networks (MICrONS) Project has built the most detailed wiring diagram of a mammalian brain to date. Simulation/emulation fidelity over time.summary: Fixed 2024 FlyVis benchmark: physiological contrast preference was not used to fit these models. This is task-specific validation, not whole-brain emulation fidelity.

plots.title: FlyVis: correct contrast preference
plots.scope: Same 32 experimentally characterized cell-type/compartment labels. Ensemble median 32/32=100%; task-optimal single model 30/32=93.75%. No longitudinal trend.

points.label: FlyVis ensemble median
points.sourceTitle: Connectome-constrained networks predict neural activity across the fly visual system
points.quote: the median flash response index (FRI) across the ensemble predicts the correct ON- and OFF-preferred contrast selectivity for all 32 cell types for which contrast selectivity has been experimentally established (terminals of CT1 in the medulla and lobula are listed as CT1(M10) and CT1(Lo1)). This is also the case for the model with the best task performance (task-optimal model), which correctly predicts the preferred contrast of 30 of 32 cells (Fig. 2b). We used only connectome and task constraints to construct our DMN, without any measurements of neural activity.
points.note: 32 of 32 cell-type/compartment labels; aggregated ensemble prediction, not 32 single-neuron temporal traces.

NeuroAI performance–cost frontier over t.summary: Fixed ImageNet-1K benchmark: measured accuracy versus theoretical inference energy. Energy is operation-count modeling, not measured hardware consumption or training cost.

plots.title: 2023 ImageNet performance–energy trade-off
plots.scope: Same 224×224 benchmark; 32-bit operations at 45 nm. 5 spiking configurations and 1 non-spiking baseline. Selected paper rows, not a global Pareto frontier.

Demonstrated applications enabled by con.summary: A categorical evidence timeline of selected synaptic-connectome research applications—not an impact score or a deployment count.

timeline.scope: AI benchmark demonstration and biological validation are separate evidence categories. Publication dates, not first-use dates. Functional-MRI clinical trials are excluded from this synaptic-connectome view.

events.label: Worm-connectome image classifier
events.sourceTitle: Caenorhabditis elegans Connectomes of both Sexes as Image Classifiers
events.quote: For the MNIST classification task, the hermaphrodite network showed 99.6% and the male network showed 99.5% accuracy after roughly 15,000 iterations We used the data from WormWiring, a website hosting the nematode connectome data mapped from electron microscope images [ 13 ]. We downloaded the latest versions of structural connectomes for both hermaphrodite and adult male C. elegans from the website [ 14 ]. The network structures of two sexes
events.note: Research benchmark demonstration, not deployment or causal proof of general AI advantage. Worm synaptic graph transformed to a DAG; neurons implemented as convolutional units.

events.label: Connectome-predicted feeding circuitry validated in flies
events.sourceTitle: A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing
events.quote: In addition, using the model to activate neurons in the feeding region of the *Drosophila* brain predicts those that elicit motor neuron firing5—a testable hypothesis that we validate by optogenetic activation and behavioural studies.
events.note: A demonstrated mechanistic research application; not a therapy, BCI or deployed AI product. Included as its own basic-science category rather than claiming clinical impact.

Demonstrated applications enabled by con.gapReason: No synaptic-connectome-enabled clinical therapy or deployed BCI is established by this evidence.
